span.span: In a variant of a KSVZ-style axion model, five heavy vector-like fermions are introduced, each with different Peccei-Quinn charges for left- and right-handed components (XL,XR)(X_{L},X_{R}). Their Standard Model gauge quantum numbers and PQ charges are:

Here QQ is the electric charge Q=T3+YQ=T_{3}+Y, where T3T_{3} is the third component of weak isospin and YY is the hypercharge, and we work entirely in Standard Model hypercharge normalization. T⁡(r)T(r) denotes the SU(3) Dynkin index and d⁡(r)d(r) the representation dimension. For the SU(3) representation 𝟏𝟎\mathbf{10}, take T⁡(𝟏𝟎)=152T(\mathbf{10})=\tfrac{15}{2}.

Using the chiral PQ charge difference (XL−XR)(X_{L}-X_{R}) as the weight for each Weyl fermion, compute the ratio E/NE/N (electromagnetic to color anomaly coefficients) and give your answer in lowest-term fractional form.
: Sums the individual color anomaly contributions to obtain the total color anomaly N=N1+N2+N3+N4+N5=654N=N_{1}+N_{2}+N_{3}+N_{4}+N_{5}=\tfrac{65}{4}.
